description: General framework for epidemiological compartmental models. All similar diseases should abide by the same structural types. Used for completeness (typed compartments) and uncertainty (parameter distribution families). Not disease-specific — hints toward the right model shape without copying another model.

vector_borne.hint: Vector-borne models should contain animal/vector compartments (e.g. mosquitoes) and host compartments. Biting rate and vector mortality are typical parameters.

std.hint: STD models should contain sexual contact structure (e.g. partner acquisition, mixing). Contact rate and partnership duration are typical parameters.

airborne.hint: Airborne transmission models typically use SEIR or SIR structure. Transmission rate, incubation rate, and recovery rate are standard.

waterborne.hint: Waterborne models often include an environmental compartment (e.g. water reservoir). Contact with reservoir and decay rate are typical.

generic.hint: Minimal SIR/SEIR structure when model type is unknown.

transmission.hint: Transmission rates are typically positive and often lognormally distributed in the literature.

recovery.hint: Recovery rate (e.g. gamma) is positive; inverse is duration of infection.

mortality.hint: Death rates are small and positive; high uncertainty in many settings.

contact.hint: Contact rates and biting rates are positive.

other.hint: Default: uniform around point estimate ±50% when type unknown.
